_about: Why Dana does each thing in the game, in her own words, and what each loop feeds. The counter out front is the point; everything else is how a stranger on the corner becomes a regular. Read by the clipboard, the results card and the how-to-play page.
premise: Laid off on a Tuesday. The garage opened on a Wednesday with a counter out front and nobody at it. The street does not know the name on the door yet. Rent does. Every job is somebody who will.

loops.title: Packing
loops.dana: You handle somebody's whole life in an afternoon. Pack it right and they trust you with the thing they care about. Trust is what fills a counter.
loops.feeds: A neat pack earns the tip; a tipped client remembers the name on the box.
loops.marge: Nobody remembers a cheap mover. They remember the one who padded the clock.

loops.title: The drive
loops.dana: The truck is the only advert I can afford. Every street it rolls down is a street that has seen the name.
loops.feeds: Honk at the people on the kerb and they look up; the ones who look up find the counter.
loops.marge: Keep it slow and keep it seen. A lorry that nobody notices is a lorry that works for free.

loops.title: Unpacking and placing
loops.dana: The room I leave behind is the one they tell their friends about. The right room, the right wall, the chair where the light is.
loops.feeds: A job with every piece in the right room sends the client to the counter with a friend.
loops.marge: You are not placing furniture. You are placing the next conversation about you.

loops.title: The counter
loops.dana: This is the point of all of it. The people I moved come in for a coffee because they know where I am now.
loops.feeds: Every name in the network shortens the wait for the next face at the till.
loops.marge: A shop is a room people come back to. Give them a reason and a seat.

loops.title: The computer
loops.dana: Rent does not wait for the next move. Buying low on the market and selling when the line goes up keeps the lights on between jobs.
loops.feeds: Cash between jobs; the odd piece that makes the counter look like a shop.
loops.marge: Trade keeps you fed. Jobs make you known. You need both, and you need them in that order some weeks.

loops.title: The workbench
loops.dana: A chipped thing mended is a client who comes back. Repairs are reputation you can hold in your hand.
loops.feeds: Mending what a move scuffed keeps the tip and the client.
loops.marge: Fix it before they notice and they tell nobody. Fix it after and they tell everybody how well.

loops.title: The back room
loops.dana: When the till is empty and the rent is due, Sal's work is money tonight. Nobody at the counter asks where it came from. Until they do.
loops.feeds: Money without faces; heat that keeps the regulars away.
loops.marge: I am not going to tell you what to do. I will tell you the regulars can smell it.

loops.title: The Movers' League
loops.dana: The bigger shop needs the bigger name. The league is where the name gets made.
loops.feeds: Rank opens the bigger offices and the clients who pay for a reputation.
loops.marge: Points are just people who would say your name if asked. Earn enough and they stop needing to be asked.

loops.title: A life of her own
loops.dana: Pickle in the cab. A room that is mine. A first million that is a number on a whiteboard until it is not.
loops.feeds: The reason to want any of this on a Tuesday.
loops.marge: Buy the dog first. The dog tips better than the accountant.

loops.title: The ladder of offices
loops.dana: Each office is a bigger window on a busier street. From a roll-up door to a corner with my name on the glass.
loops.feeds: A bigger window is a bigger counter and more of the street walking past it.
loops.marge: You will miss the garage. Everybody does. Go anyway.

loops.name: The long haul
loops.dana: Somebody in Charleston needs a mover from Columbia and the name travels with the truck. Two hundred miles of interstate is two hundred miles of people reading the side of it.
loops.feeds: Pay by the mile, and a client in a city the counter could never reach on its own.
loops.marge: Fill up before you go. Nobody tips the mover who ran out of gas at Orangeburg.

visitor_lines: You moved my whole life in an afternoon. The least I can do is buy a coffee.

I told the whole street where you were. You're welcome.
Nothing broke. I'm here to say so in person.
The chair's where you put it. We tried moving it. It went back.
Knew you'd be here. Marge said the kettle's always on.
Came to see the counter you kept going on about.
